subtopics.title: Free Fall and the Equations of Motion

questions.question: A projectile is defined as an object on which:
options: The only force acting is the gravitational force
Gravity and air resistance act together

questions.question: A brick is dropped from 19,6 m. Ignoring air resistance, it reaches the ground after:
The word "dropped" in a projectile question tells you that:
options: The object falls at constant velocity

questions.question: While a ball is rising after leaving the hand, its acceleration is:
options: 9,8 m·s⁻² upward, decreasing as it rises
Zero, because it is slowing down

subtopics.title: Thrown Upward — Symmetry and the Top of the Flight

questions.question: At the highest point of its flight, a ball thrown straight up has:
options: Zero velocity and acceleration of 9,8 m·s⁻² downward
Maximum velocity and acceleration of 9,8 m·s⁻² upward

questions.question: A ball is thrown up at 19,6 m·s⁻¹. Its maximum height above the hand is:
That same ball returns to the throwing height moving at:
options: 19,6 m·s⁻¹ downward — the same speed it left with
9,8 m·s⁻¹ downward — half the speed it left with
A speed that cannot be found without more information
39,2 m·s⁻¹ downward — twice the speed it left with

questions.question: A ball rises 19,6 m and returns to the hand. Its total DISTANCE and total DISPLACEMENT are:

subtopics.title: The Three Graphs — Dropped, Thrown Up and Bouncing

questions.question: For the entire flight of any projectile, the acceleration-time graph is:
options: A horizontal line at 9,8 m·s⁻² downward

questions.question: On a velocity-time graph, the moment of maximum height is where the graph:
The parabola on a position-time graph of a ball thrown upward represents:
options: The curved path the ball follows through the air
The force acting on the ball
The ball's height plotted against time — the ball itself moves straight up and down

questions.question: On the velocity-time graph of a bouncing ball, each bounce appears as:
options: An almost vertical jump to a smaller value in the opposite direction
A gradual curve back to zero
A change in the gradient of the line

questions.question: The gradient of a position-time graph gives the object's:
The area between a velocity-time graph and the time axis gives the:
options: Displacement, with areas below the axis counting negative

questions.question: A ball is thrown up at 19,6 m·s⁻¹. The triangle under its velocity-time graph from 0 to 2 s has area ½ × 2 × 19,6. This number is the ball's:
A horizontal tangent on a position-time graph means the object is:
options: Momentarily at rest — for a projectile, at maximum height

questions.question: A ball is thrown up at 19,6 m·s⁻¹. One second later its speed is:
If a ball takes 3 s to reach its highest point, the time for the whole flight back to the throwing height is:
options: 6 s, because time up equals time down
3 s, because the trip only counts once
It cannot be found without the throwing speed

questions.question: At the very top of the flight, the speed is zero. The acceleration is:
options: Also zero, since the ball is at rest
9,8 m·s⁻² upward, holding the ball up
Smaller than 9,8 m·s⁻², since the ball is far from the ground
Still 9,8 m·s⁻² downward — gravity never pauses

subtopics.title: The Ball's Diary — Three Graphs, One Story

questions.question: The rainbow-shaped curve on the height-time graph of a thrown ball shows:
options: The curved path of the ball through the air
Height against time, for a ball moving straight up and down

questions.question: The speed diary — the velocity-time graph — of a projectile is a straight line because:
options: The ball moves in a straight line
Gravity removes the same amount of velocity every second

questions.question: When the velocity-time line crosses zero, the position-time graph is:
options: At its peak — the two graphs agree on the top of the flight
Crossing zero at the same moment

questions.question: A negative value on the velocity-time graph, with upward taken as positive, means the ball is:
On a bouncing ball's velocity-time graph, every crossing of the time axis marks:
options: A top of flight — the ball momentarily still in mid-air

questions.question: After each bounce the ball leaves the floor slower than it arrived because:
options: Some kinetic energy is lost as sound and deformation in the bounce
Gravity gets stronger with every bounce
Air resistance acts only during bounces

questions.question: The straight segments of the bouncing ball's velocity-time graph are all parallel because:
options: The ball always falls from the same height
Each bounce restores the ball's energy
Between bounces the acceleration is always 9,8 m·s⁻² downward

questions.question: The sudden, almost vertical jumps on the graph occur when the ball:
options: Is in contact with the floor and reverses direction
